intro: Some of the oldest written words of Anatolia are waiting for you here. This is the Kayseri Archaeology Museum in Kayseri province, opened in 1969. It holds the finds of the Kültepe-Kanesh excavation, including the cuneiform tablets and clay envelopes of the Assyrian merchants.
history: The heart of the museum is the Kültepe-Kanesh excavation, twenty kilometres north-east of the city. There, in the second millennium BC, Assyrian merchants founded a karum, and it produced Anatolia's earliest written documents. What did they write about? Business: trade contracts and promissory notes.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Kültepe tablets and their clay envelopes and seals, then move on to the Hittite works and the Roman sculpture.
facts: Did you know? The Kültepe tablets came out of the ground inside clay envelopes. A summary of the contract was written on the envelope, which was sealed and broken open only if there was a dispute. The Kültepe-Kanesh tablets are Anatolia's earliest written documents, and every one of them is a trade record, a contract or a note of debt.
outro: This brings our journey through the Kayseri Archaeology Museum to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
